clue.text: Notoriously disorderly students take year out from intimidating teacher with stick

indicators.note: with 'take' before it, 'take year out from' tells us to remove the letter for year from the next word

parts.note: intimidating others is bullying them
a don is a university teacher
a club is a heavy stick

explanation.surface: A rowdy student group gets rid of a bullying lecturer, and a stick features somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'take ... out from' instruction removes Y from BULLYING, leaving BULLING. The Bullingdon Club is an Oxford University dining society known for wealthy members' rowdy behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford dining society is notorious for its members trashing restaurants, so its undergraduates are a byword for wild behaviour.

clue.text: Height fashionable during topless spring craze

indicators.note: one piece sits during, that is inside, the other
the word for spring loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: a spring forward is a lunge
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A tall figure in vogue during a summery season of bare-chested madness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the first letter off the spring and 'during' puts the other pieces inside what is left. 'craze' is a verb here, to drive mad, not a fad.
explanation.definitionFit: To craze someone is to send them mad, and to unhinge them is to unbalance their mind.

clue.text: Something to drink with red meat course nearly cooked

parts.note: lamb is a red meat

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked over into a new order
nearly means the word for course loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink served alongside lamb when the main course is almost ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final E of COURSE and 'cooked' rearranges COURS to RUSCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red Italian wine, a type of drink.

clue.text: Anorak, one worn by patrician Latin poet

indicators.note: the patrician's letter and the garment-like pieces are layered together, one inside the other

parts.note: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, a nerd
U means upper-class, the class of patricians
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A Roman aristocrat wearing a hooded waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper-class) goes inside NERD + A. Pablo Neruda was a Chilean poet, so 'Latin' means Latin American, not ancient Roman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Neruda was a Nobel-winning poet from Chile, in Latin America.

clue.text: No boarder gets new note in unofficial Irish anthem

indicators.note: the pupil gets, or takes in, the extra letters

parts.note: a day boy is a pupil who goes home each night, not a boarder
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A day pupil picks up a fresh tune that becomes an unofficial Irish song.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a day boy attends lessons but lives at home, unlike a boarder. 'Danny Boy' is a ballad sung as an unofficial Irish anthem.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballad set to the Londonderry Air is widely sung as a national song by the Irish diaspora.

clue.text: Henry's in agreeable, comfortable position

indicators.note: Henry's letter is in the word for agreeable

parts.note: nice means agreeable
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry is in a pleasant, cosy situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a role or place that suits someone well, a snug position.

clue.text: Ancient joke after Newton John's incarcerated

indicators.note: the pieces are locked up inside the word for John

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: the joke comes after Newton's letter

parts.note: N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: An old gag about the singer Olivia Newton-John being jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invokes the singer Olivia Newton-John, but Newton gives N and John is a lavatory, LOO, which holds N + GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long ago happened in ancient times.

clue.text: Eccentric orbits hold level closer to 27

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are put out of order

parts.note: a tier is a level

explanation.surface: Wayward planetary orbits keep to a flat plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges ORBITS HOLD to give BLOODTHIRS, then TIER is added. Entry 27 is VAMPIRE, so 'closer to 27' means more like a vampire.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampires crave blood, so being more like one means being more bloodthirsty.

clue.text: Engineer may best compute future transport order?

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the following letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: An engineer might be the person best placed to work out how teleporting will work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' looks like Scotty, the Star Trek engineer, but it rearranges MAY BEST COMPUTE. The catchphrase is what Captain Kirk tells Scotty when he wants to be teleported.
explanation.definitionFit: In Star Trek, set in the future, this is the command to the engineer to teleport someone aboard.

clue.text: I may enable second autopsy without bones being cut

parts.note: ex means without, as in shares sold ex dividend

indicators.note: being cut means the word for bones loses its end

parts.note: humeri are the upper-arm bones

explanation.surface: A pathologist doing a repeat post-mortem without cutting through bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being cut' trims the last letter from HUMERI. Someone who digs up a body allows a second post-mortem to be done.
explanation.definitionFit: A body must be dug up from its grave before a further post-mortem can be carried out.

clue.text: It's impossible for me, dismissing thousands from front and centre of Speyside distillery

indicators.note: dismissing means the letters for thousands are sent away from the front and centre of the name

parts.note: Knockando is a whisky distillery on Speyside in Scotland
K stands for a thousand, so two are thousands

explanation.surface: Someone declares they cannot manage something, turning away thousands from a Scottish whisky distillery.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Ks of KNOCKANDO are at the front and the centre, as the clue says. Speyside is a whisky-making area of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase is a refusal meaning the speaker cannot do what is asked.

clue.text: Damn Fairy Liquid does all sorts of jobs

definitions.note: the definition is a description of what the person does, standing for a noun

indicators.note: liquid means fluid and shapeless, so the letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A brand of washing-up liquid is praised for handling every kind of chore.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairy Liquid is a famous British washing-up liquid brand, but 'Liquid' rearranges DAMN FAIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A man Friday is a general helper or factotum, after Robinson Crusoe's servant.

clue.text: Chicagoan high roller, perhaps accompanying hoofer?

parts.note: the El is Chicago's elevated railway, whose trains roll high above the street
and means along with, accompanying

explanation.surface: A Chicago gambler with a dancer in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high roller' suggests a big gambler but means a train on raised track. 'hoofer' is usually a dancer; here it is a hoofed animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, an animal with hooves.

clue.text: European left page a lot

parts.note: the verso is the left-hand page of an open book

explanation.surface: A European leaves a page behind in large quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal intensifier meaning very much, as in thanks ever so.

clue.text: Sooty friend enters so as to be revealed indeed

indicators.note: the friend's name goes into the other word

parts.note: forth means out into view, as when something is brought forth and revealed
Soo is the panda friend of Sooty, the glove puppet bear of British children's television

explanation.surface: A puppet's pal enters so that the truth comes out, truly.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a long-running British children's TV glove puppet bear; his friend is a panda. 'forth' is used as an adverb, out into the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic word for truly or in truth.

clue.text: Produce thread for web enclosing skin? He can

definitions.note: the definition points back to the rest of the clue: the superhero is the man who can do this

indicators.note: the word for producing thread encloses the word for skin

parts.note: spiders spin thread for their webs
derma is the skin

explanation.surface: Asking who can spin a web around skin, and answering that he can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He can' reads back over the whole clue: the hero is the one able to spin webs. 'enclosing' puts the skin word inside the spinning word.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book superhero can shoot web threads like a spider.

clue.text: I'd like to think rally meets in shelter

indicators.note: the mixed letters go in the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

indicators.note: rally means regroup or reassemble, so these letters are regrouped

explanation.surface: A rally gathers in a sheltered spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rally' reads as a noun, a mass meeting, but it is the anagram signal on 'meets'; 'in' puts the result inside the shelter word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is what someone says when pausing to consider or recall something.

clue.text: Someone jostling after turning up in child's play

indicators.note: the jostler comes after the turned word
turning means the small word is read backwards

parts.note: a shover is someone who pushes and jostles

explanation.surface: A jostler turns up at a game for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' applies to 'up' alone, and 'after' places the jostler behind it; 'child's play' means an easy task.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that is child's play is easy, a walkover.

clue.text: Spilling one's guts in pages in location of Kent University

indicators.note: the pages sit in the location

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of the UK: SE UK

explanation.surface: Someone confesses everything in pages written at the University of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spilling one's guts' looks like confessing, but means literal disembowelling. Kent is a county in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Seppuku is Japanese ritual suicide by cutting open the belly.

clue.text: Cure occupant of bed?

definitions.meaning: to cure fish is to preserve it by smoking
kip is British slang for sleep, so a sleeper is one who kips

explanation.surface: Is there a remedy for whoever is in this bed?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' here means preserving fish by smoking or salting, not healing.
explanation.definitionFit: To kipper is to cure a herring by splitting and smoking it; one who kips is a sleeper in bed.

clue.text: Superior one carried by woman before giving birth?

indicators.note: the woman carries the letter for one inside her

parts.note: before giving birth a woman is a mum-to-be, a pre-mum
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman is carrying a baby, a superior one.
explanation.walkthrough: PREMUM (pre-mum, a woman who will soon be a mother) is an invented word, hence the question mark; it carries I.
explanation.definitionFit: Premium goods are of top quality, superior.

clue.text: Deathtrap writer's upset, giving whimper

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: Ira Levin wrote the thriller play Deathtrap

explanation.surface: The playwright of Deathtrap is distressed and starts whimpering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LEVIN'S over, reading it upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To snivel is to sniff and cry feebly, a whine or whimper.

clue.text: Something to chew over, accepting holy god

indicators.note: the chewed thing accepts the holy word inside it

parts.note: cud is what cows chew over again
pi is British school slang for pious or holy

explanation.surface: Food for thought welcomes a pious deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chew over' suggests something to think about, but it is a cow's cud. 'pi' is British informal for sanctimonious.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid is the Roman god of love.

clue.text: Investigate victor in strike

indicators.note: the letter for victor goes in the word for strike

parts.note: dele is the proof-reader's mark meaning delete, strike out
V is victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A winner is caught up in an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' looks like a walkout but means strike out, DELE in proofreading.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig into or research a matter.

clue.text: Ruffles all the many in Paris

parts.note: tous is French for all, with 'in Paris' applying here too
les is the French plural article, the word used for the many

explanation.surface: Every one of many gets ruffled in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells us to use French: tous les means all the.
explanation.definitionFit: To tousle hair is to rumple or dishevel it.

clue.text: Someone exploiting voltage and energy represented by current in relevant unit

parts.note: V is the symbol for voltage

indicators.note: the energy letter is represented by, replaced with, the current letter

parts.note: the ampere is the unit of current, so it is relevant to current
E is the symbol for energy
I is the physics symbol for current

explanation.surface: A technical description of an electrical exploiter in physics terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented by' swaps the first E of the unit for the current symbol, and V goes in front. A vampire, figuratively, preys on others.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire, figuratively, is a person who preys on or exploits others.

clue.text: I know poker player's weakness, tucking into year-old, rotten meringue

indicators.note: the weakness is tucked into the other letters

parts.note: Y for year and O for old

indicators.note: rotten means spoilt, so the letters are spoilt into a new order

parts.note: a tell is an involuntary sign that gives away a poker player's hand

explanation.surface: A poker player shows his weakness by tucking into a stale meringue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' rearranges 'meringue' and 'tucking into' puts the poker weakness inside after the year-old letters; a tell is an unconscious giveaway of a bluff.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic agreement meaning the speaker already knows that all too well.
